title: Implementing a recommender
goals: Handle ties and no eligible options

prerequisite.prompt: An option violates a hard duration limit but has the best score. Should it win?
prerequisite.answer: No. Filter by the hard constraint before ranking.

vocabulary: A procedure that suggests options using a stated policy
Two options have the same comparison score
The same inputs and rules produce the same result
Evidence describing how a result was obtained

blocks.text: Build a fictional activity recommender using last week's score. Require duration at most a supplied limit. On a tie choose the alphabetically first name. This makes the outcome reproducible rather than dependent on input order. Assume unique names and validated numeric fields.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
def recommend(items, limit):
    best = None
    best_score = None
    for item in items:
        if item["minutes"] <= limit:
            score = 2 * item["fun"] + item["learning"]
            if (best is None or score > best_score
                or (score == best_score and item["name"] < best)):
                best = item["name"]
                best_score = score
    return best

items = [{"name": "B", "fun": 3, "learning": 2, "minutes": 10},
         {"name": "A", "fun": 2, "learning": 4, "minutes": 9}]
print(recommend(items, 10))

blocks.title: Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The function prints nothing; the caller prints A. best starts as None to mean no eligible option found. Python short-circuits or: when best is None, later comparisons in that condition need not run. After selecting an item, best_score is numeric. An empty list or no eligible item returns None.

blocks.label: Predict the result if the list order is reversed, and if the limit is 8.

blocks.text: Updating best on score >= best_score makes the last tied item win, so reordering can change results. Use the explicit name comparison for ties. Test both orders and a no-match case after the repair.

The recommendation follows a written scoring policy. It does not learn preferences, prove learning benefit or authorize an action. Display the chosen rule and let a person review whether an option is suitable.

blocks.label: Write a one-sentence explanation of X winning without calling it objectively best.

workbook.title: Trace selection
workbook.prompt: Why does A win the worked example even though B is processed first?
workbook.answer: Both score 8 and qualify; A is alphabetically first under the tie rule.

workbook.title: Handle no match
workbook.prompt: State recommend([], 10) and the worked items with limit 8.
workbook.answer: Both return None; the caller should display no eligible option.

workbook.title: Repair order dependence
workbook.prompt: A tied selection changes after reversing input order. Identify the likely missing policy and test.
workbook.answer: An explicit deterministic tie rule is missing or incorrect. Apply alphabetical name order and rerun both orders.

workbook.title: Implement independently
workbook.prompt: Use the function with X (fun 4, learning 1, minutes 12), Y (3,3,10), Z (5,5,13), limit 12. Predict the winner, reverse the list and retest. Also test limit 9.
workbook.answer: X and Y score 9; Z is excluded. X wins alphabetically in either order. Limit 9 returns None.

workbook.title: Explain the result
workbook.prompt: Write a one-sentence explanation of X winning without calling it objectively best.
workbook.answer: X meets the 12-minute limit and ties for highest eligible score 9; the alphabetical tie rule selects X.
